The stamper itself,  is made up of two parts. The squishy thing to actually transfer the stamp to your nail, and the tube thing that holds it. Very disappointed in this one. No matter what I do or which polishes I use, it absolutely refuses to pick up anything. I've been stamping for a good 6 years, so I think I've got the technique down by now. I've tried both stamping polishes and just regular polishes, but nothing. After about an hour of running through every single polish I own (and several nail plates, in case it was an issue with the pattern), I gave up and primed it like I would a regular stamper, buffing and acetone. Of course,

Kinda disappointed in this product. I tried using it with several polishes and the image would not pick up. (I have been stamping for about 2 years now and consider myself very experienced). So i gave it a little sanding with my nail file and now it works perfectly. I love that it picks up every image, the downside is that its a bit blurry and no longer useful for what i bought it for.... to be able to see the image as i was placing in my nail.

Love the clear stamper for this, especially with placing images right where you want them! This is the second purchase of this stamper, the first one got too cloudy, I never used acetone on it either, I always did clean up with a lint roller. The second purchase has still been holding up well though!

I have tried everything, will not pick up the image. Doesn't matter if stamping polish or regular. I keep reading the jelly stompers don't need primed. Tried anyway, both acetone and file prime method, will not pick up the image. Very disappointed.

The Malloon Clear Nail Art Stamper is a great little tool for nail art! I've been using it for over a year now and it's a great way to add a design or a pop to your nails!!  It does come with a scraper. The scraper does dirty easily but is also very easy to clean up. The only thing I will say about the stamp itself is to make sure you keep it clean! I wipe after every stamp transfer and keep the stamper in a bag. It will collect dust quickly and the rubber piece can be difficult to get dust off

This is a must buy if youre into nail stamping. This works wonderfully to pick up the nail polish design and even better that you can see exactly where the design will be placed on the nail. The little rubber head sits perfectly in the stanping unit and doesnt come of during use. However, it does come off easy if you need to pull it off to clean. A quick wipe with a small cotton ball dampened with nail polish remover is enough for me to clean it. Ived used mine over 15 times and it stayed clear

I'm not sure if it just mine, but I can't get ANYTHING to stick to this. I have used konad Polish, and other brands I bought on Amazon, and I'm lucky if I get an outline to stick to this stamper. Frustrating, and I don't use it at all. The scraper is "meh" but I don't think many scrapers that are this cheap are the greatest. I also wiped it off (definitely didn't use pressure) and now there's a tiny rip in the rubber stamper part.

This stamper I use the most. So much that is cloudy at the top (because I was using acetone instead of nail polish remover) but it doesn't affect me from seeing the design when I put it on my nail. The rubber piece has held up also. My cat got it one time and I was so afraid that it was going to have a gash in it from my cats teeth but I couldn't find anything. Not even a hole!! Which is fantastic!!!!!

At first I was wondering why my stamper didn't pick up the designs WELL I decided to look up a how to on YouTube and then I was able to use it.  I switched my nail Polish also so anyone having problems might want to change polishes, just figured I would share that. I got a bottle of Broadway nail gel strong at the dollar market for 2$ and it worked perfectly! !! I love my stamper might I add also :-)

claims.text: Many reviewers report the stamper fails to pick up images, even with stamping polishes and experience.
Several reviewers find the clear stamper helpful for seeing exactly where to place designs.
Some reviewers say priming the stamper (with alcohol, filing, or buffing) was needed before it worked well.
Reviewers describe the stamper as squishy or gooshy and easy to use.
A few reviewers mention durability issues, such as the tip falling off or the stamper falling apart.
